items.title: Headlines for November 20, 2026 | Democracy Now!
items.excerpt: ## Senate Rejects War Powers Resolution to Limit Trump’s Attacks on Iran Nov 20, 2026 The Senate rejected a war powers resolution on Thursday that would have directed President Trump to seek congressional approval before resuming attacks on Iran. The resolution failed on a vote of 51-48. Three Republicans voted in favor, while Pennsylvania Democratic Senator John Fetterman voted in opposition. The House approved the resolution in September. Both the House and Senate previously approved a war powers resolution back in June, but President Trump largely ignored it. Thursday’s failed vote in the Senate came after Democratic House leader Hakeem Jeffries suggested he would not block funding for attacks on Iran in the government funding package due by December 11. Meanwhile, a Pentagon official said Thursday the cost of the war on Iran has topped $48 billion. That figure does not include damage to U.S. bases, the cost of providing healthcare to hundreds of injured troops or the tens of billions of dollars in higher fuel costs triggered by the war. ## Senate Passes Permitting Reform Bill with Support of 14 Democrats, Including Leader Chuck Schumer Nov 20, 2026 The Senate has approved a permitting reform bill that would weaken environmental laws to speed approval of new housing, roads, energy projects and other infrastructure. While the bill would make it easier to build new transmission lines and wind and solar farms, it would also speed construction of fossil fuel power plants and new data centers, including on public lands. Meanwhile, Native leaders and advocacy groups strongly opposed the legislation, saying it would weaken tribal sovereignty and threaten cultural and sacred sites. This is Oregon Democratic Senator Jeff Merkley, who voted “no.” > Sen. Jeff Merkley: “First, it makes it a lot easier to build data centers. Did anybody notice data centers were a big issue in this most recent election? Here we come right in after the election, and we’re going to pass a bill that makes it easier to do data centers by striking down tools that states have when they decide they do not want to have a data center because it threatens key clean air or clean water issues.” Despite those objections, the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, known as BAAJA, passed on a vote of 62-33 with 14 Democrats in favor, including Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer. In a statement, Food & Water Watch said, “Sen. Schumer’s alignment with Republicans over a majority of his own Democratic caucus in voting to advance this terrible pro-polluter, pro-data center permitting bill is all the reason needed to demand that Schumer step down as leader of the Senate Democrats.” The bill now goes to the House and is expected to be voted on the week after next. ## Climate Activists Condemn “Slimmed-Down” COP31 Draft Text That Makes No Reference to Fossil Fuels Nov 20, 2026 Here at the COP31 U.N. climate summit, negotiators published a “slimmed-down” draft text on Thursday that stripped out any reference to fossil fuels, or ending their use. Instead, the document promotes carbon capture and storage, an unproven technology that critics say will never have a meaningful impact on the climate crisis. Activists at the COP are demanding more financing to help poorer countries adapt to a warming world. This is Iona Stewart of the climate action group Global Witness. ... ## Russian Attacks Kill 8 After Ukraine Bombs Bridge Connecting Russia to Occupied Crimea Nov 20, 2026 In Ukraine, officials say eight people were killed and dozens injured overnight, as Russia launched a massive drone and missile attack. In Kyiv, Russian bombs struck three ⁠bridges over the Dnipro River. Meanwhile, in Kharkiv, a Russian drone damaged a hospital, wounding four people. The Russian attacks came after Ukraine bombed the Kerch Bridge, the only link between mainland Russia and Russian-annexed Crimea. Engineers say it could take years for Russia to repair the damage. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky defended the bridge strike and warned of further action. > President Volodymyr Zelensky: “We have long been telling Russia: Enough of striking bridges, our cities and villages, Ukraine’s energy infrastructure, railways and grain ships. Enough of this war. But every time, Russia chooses a new escalation.” Meanwhile, Poland’s military said it was investigating a suspected violation of its airspace by Russia near Poland’s border with Ukraine, after an unidentified object crash-landed this morning.

items.title: Fed’s Cook says rate hikes needed to lower high inflation By Reuters
items.excerpt: Nov 20 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook on Friday made a case for more interest rate hikes, saying the US central bank’s current policy rate is not high enough to deal with inflation levels she views with "great concern." "In a different environment, the (Federal Open Market) Committee could afford to be patient, but I continue to believe that in this economic climate we do not have that luxury," given how high inflation is and for how long it has been above the Fed’s 2% target, Cook said in the text of a speech to be presented at a central bank conference in Chile. Cook said the quarter-percentage-point rate hike the Fed delivered at its September 15-16 policy meeting was not enough to moderate current levels of inflation. What’s more, "inflation data received since the September rate increase, including reports last week, fail to provide me with sufficient evidence that inflation is returning to a sustainable path," she said. "There is little evidence inflation is declining." Cook, who voted for a rate hike at that meeting, was one of two Fed officials who dissented over the Fed’s decision last month to leave its policy rate in the 3.75%-4.00% range. Officials at the October 27-28 meeting signaled that inflation remained too high then even as they refrained from action. Regarding her dissent in October, Cook said, "My vote reflected the urgency I feel to tackle inflation," which "has been above target for more than five and a half years, and every additional day poses greater risk that price- and wage-setters will adjust their inflation expectations upward." RATE HIKE EXPECTED IN DECEMBER A wide range of Fed officials in recent weeks have signaled support for more rate hikes, and financial markets broadly expect the Fed to raise rates at its December 8-9 meeting and to follow that move with more increases next year. Most Fed officials have made a case for gradual action to lower inflation, arguing that doing so would give the economy time to adjust to the rise in borrowing costs. But some, concerned with the most recent inflation data, have speculated that aggressive moves may be needed to bring price pressures to heel. Cook on Friday said the risk of not acting fast enough to lower inflation could bring more pain later. "Waiting longer to implement rate increases risks getting behind the curve," she said. "If we fall behind, additional and larger rate increases may be required later to catch up, which could increase stress on our financial system and have unnecessarily damaging effects on American households." The Fed governor noted that financial conditions remain accommodative and are not providing the needed level of restraint on the economy. Cook, however, was upbeat on the economy. She said growth is "strong and accelerating" and that the job market remains "solid."

About 1 in 6 consumers in the University of Michigan survey said in October 2026 that they expect prices to rise 15% or more over the next year, the same share as a year earlier. The typical household is far calmer, and getting calmer. Median year-ahead inflation expectations “plunged from 4.7% last month to 3.7% this month,” University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers director Joanne Hsu said in the final November reading released Friday. That gap between the most frightened consumers and the data is what anyone setting prices or pay should watch. In the late 1970s, expectations that came loose from the numbers ended up feeding the inflation.

In the published text he calls rapid AI adoption a shock that hits demand and supply at different times. Optimism about the technology "has been boosting business investment in data centers, advanced computing equipment, and related products," he said. "Currently, the AI buildout is exerting upward pressure on demand and inflation." Source The upside comes later. "In the future, advancements in productivity could exert downward pressure on inflation while continuing to support growth," Jefferson said. He also warned that "AI could cause some job displacement, a meaningful challenge for affected households." He gave no signal about the next rate decision.

items.title: Music News Nov. 20: Grand Theft Auto VI soundtrack, Beabadoobee announces new album
items.excerpt: ### Beabadoobee Goes Bananas 4 Cats on New Album and Song (Pitchfork) Beabadoobee released her latest record, Pylon, just two months ago, and she’s already announced that she has another one on the way! It’s called Bananas 4 Cats, and Beabadoobee said in a release that she “just needed to write an album like this after Pylon.” She also said it happened naturally, that she felt inspired, and made another album. The announcement also comes with the release of a new song called “No Punctuation” that she’s shared snippets of on social media over the past couple of years, but only recently started playing live. Bananas 4 Cats will be out February 19. ... ### Lindsey Buckingham, Keith Richards, Jason Sudeikis, PinkPantheress and more confirmed as ‘GTA 6’ radio hosts (NME) Grand Theft Auto VI is officially out, and it has a huge musical component to it. There are multiple radio stations you can listen to in the game, and when you do, you’ll hear some famous voices guiding you along. Lindsey Buckingham from Fleetwood Mac, Weird Al Yankovic, Gloria Estefan, The Dare, PinkPantheress, Keith Richards, Bad Bunny, Lana Del Rey and her husband Jeremy Dufrene, Chilli and T-Boz from TLC, Michael McDonald, Brigitte Nielsen, and Jason Sudeikis are all DJs on various radio stations in the game. There are also five different episodic podcasts that players can listen to as they go on their gaming adventures. ... ### ‘Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album’ Is Here: Stream the Project Featuring Dua Lipa, Playboi Carti, Lana Del Rey, Cardi B & More (Billboard) The new Grand Theft Auto video game also comes with a stellar soundtrack. Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album has 34 tracks on it that spans genres.
